newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horn sees up to 23 pct Hungary energy price rise.
newsitem.headline: Horn sees up to 23 pct Hungary energy price rise.

text.p: Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn said Hungary's energy price rise, due in January, was likely to be smaller than expected.

Horn was quoted by Hungarian Radio on Saturday as saying that energy prices would probably be raised by up to 23 percent on January 1. He was speaking to an open forum, held late on Friday in Pecs, south Hungary.

The government said in August it was postponing the price rise, previously announced for October 1, as a study by the National Energy Office (NEO) had not produced all the information needed for a decision.
The government did not say how big a rise it planned, but press reports said it was between 30 and 40 percent.
Hungary guaranteed in international agreements and laws that the regional energy supply companies in which foreign investors bought large stakes would have an eight percent profit margin from 1997.
A government commissioner is still negotiating with the foreign investors about the base of the profit margin and the energy suppliers' costs which the government would acknowledge.
The government earlier said it was likely to make its decision on the size of the price rise by the end of October.
